hero.headline:
Structures, tested
against reality.
hero.focus: Computational design and mechanics of structures under seismic loading, with embodied carbon as a design variable; current work spans superelastic NiTi systems and thin-shell form-finding and stability.

map.heading: Two directions
map.question: How do we design structural systems that perform better under real seismic demands without ignoring the material and carbon cost of achieving that performance?

directions.title: Superelastic materials and seismic systems
directions.summary: Nickel-titanium constitutive models, self-centring fuses, and frame idealisations. Residual drift, peak drift, and carbon stay in the same comparison.

directions.title: Thin-shell form, stability, and carbon
directions.summary: Form-finding, buckling, and embodied carbon for thin concrete shells. A rib layout, a thickness change, and a whole-building floor are different kinds of result.

work.heading: Selected work
work.lede: A superelastic NiTi diagrid, a form-found shell, stress-line ribs that lost an equal-volume buckling comparison, and a shell floor read as a whole building.

method.heading: How a result is earned
method.intro: One loop, used only where a project needs it. A numerical check supports a numerical claim. It is not a full-scale experiment.

steps.title: Question
steps.text: A claim that can fail: drift, buckling, a constitutive response, or a carbon saving.

steps.title: Model
steps.text: A return map, a finite-element model, a form-finding scheme, or a carbon inventory.

steps.title: Verify
steps.text: A benchmark, a tangent check, a mesh study, or a test suite, named next to the number.

steps.title: Analyse
steps.text: Seismic response, stability, or a Pareto comparison, with the result that went the wrong way kept in view.

steps.title: Design
steps.text: A fuse, a shell, or a floor, only as strong as the check underneath it.

outputs.heading: Research outputs
outputs.lede: Submitted, with the editor, preprint, and published stay in their own words. A dataset DOI is not a journal article.

tools.heading: Open a model
tools.lede: These are the public tools. ShellLab is the force-density solver in the browser. The diagrid explorer is the canopy model from the NiTi study.

about.heading: About
lines: The open questions are 3D thermomechanical shape-memory models, imperfection-sensitive shells and enriched continua, and lightweight systems where seismic performance and embodied carbon are decided together.
